writeup.1: Jones Sports Company has been making single-strap carry bags in Portland, Oregon since 1971, and the founding story is better than most because it is small. George Jones was a forty-year-old taxi driver who sewed the first bags in his basement and sold them out of the trunk of his cab. Jones still tells it that way on their own history page, and finishes the thought with a line that is hard to improve on: “Who could have known? George Jones, that’s who.”
writeup.2: What their site skips is the middle. George sold the company in 1990, and the new owners tried to make a Jones bag compete with the big manufacturers by making it less like a Jones bag. By the early 2000s the brand was effectively gone. The Lemman family and Chris Carnahan bought it in 2011, and what they bought was almost nothing: no patterns, no inventory, no factory. Matt Lemman, asked later what came with the deal: “Just the name, that was all.”
writeup.3: They reverse-engineered it from the bags that were still around Portland. Carnahan has said they gathered old ones from family and friends, and there were plenty to gather, because the bags last. They rebuilt to the original specifications in modern materials, which is why the Original still looks like the photographs from 1975 and weighs 2.9 lbs.
writeup.4: The current line runs from the $125 Original through the F-35 ripstop stand bags, the Rider cart bag, eighteen officially licensed school versions and the collaborations with PAYNTR, BEAMS and Lusso Cloud. One correction to something you will read elsewhere: Jones does not claim anywhere on its own site to have invented the single-strap carry bag.
